Baseball starter: Pythagorean expectation

Data: the Lahman Baseball Database (Sean Lahman), mirrored as CSV by Rdatasets. Credit both when you use them. Bill James's famous idea: a team's wins are predicted almost scarily well by just two numbers - runs scored and runs allowed. Let's check on 20+ years of MLB seasons. Where you have seen this: this is the Moneyball idea - the 2002 Oakland A's, the Michael Lewis book, the Brad Pitt film. A low-budget team winning by trusting numbers over gut feel.

On average a team's Pythagorean record is off by only 3.3 wins over a season.

Your turn

  • Find the biggest overachievers (won way more than their runs suggest). What did they do? (Look at one-run games.)
  • The exponent doesn't have to be 2: which exponent minimizes the error?
  • Same idea, other sports: does it work on the NFL or NHL starters in this repo?
What good looks like: you can explain your chart in one plain sentence, and name one thing it does not tell you.
